\section[anteriormente]{anteriormente — previously, earlier}

\label{lesson:ES-C538-anteriormente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for a short time ago, then the Spanish for the day before yesterday.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: anteriormente}
\textbf{anteriormente} — \textquotedblleft{}previously, earlier\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Anteriormente vivía en Madrid.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Previously she lived in Madrid.}
\end{quote}

A formal word; in speech people say \emph{antes}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{anteriormente} is built on \emph{anterior} and the ending \emph{-mente} (EtymDB). \emph{Anterior} is a learned word from Latin \emph{anterior} 'former', built on \emph{ante} 'before'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{anteriormente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{anteriormente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{anteriormente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for a short time ago, then the Spanish for the day before yesterday, then say \emph{anteriormente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does anteriormente mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Previously, earlier\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[posteriormente]{posteriormente — subsequently, later}

\label{lesson:ES-C538-posteriormente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the day before yesterday, then the Spanish for previously.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: posteriormente}
\textbf{posteriormente} — \textquotedblleft{}subsequently, later\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Posteriormente la policía detuvo al hombre.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The police later arrested the man.}
\end{quote}

A formal word, common in the news.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{posteriormente} is built on \emph{posterior} and the ending \emph{-mente} (EtymDB). \emph{Posterior} is a learned word from Latin \emph{posterior} 'later', from \emph{posterus}, built on \emph{post} 'after' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{posteriormente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{posteriormente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{posteriormente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the day before yesterday, then the Spanish for previously, then say \emph{posteriormente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does posteriormente mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Subsequently, later\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[previamente]{previamente — beforehand, previously}

\label{lesson:ES-C538-previamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for previously, then the Spanish for subsequently.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: previamente}
\textbf{previamente} — \textquotedblleft{}beforehand, previously\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hay que reservar previamente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{You have to book beforehand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{previamente} is built on \emph{previo} and the ending \emph{-mente} (EtymDB). \emph{Previo} is a learned word from Latin \emph{praevius} 'going before', built on \emph{prae} and \emph{via} 'way' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[recientemente]{recientemente — recently}

\label{lesson:ES-C538-recientemente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for subsequently, then the Spanish for beforehand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: recientemente}
\textbf{recientemente} — \textquotedblleft{}recently\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Recientemente abrieron un museo nuevo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A new museum opened recently.}
\end{quote}

Before a participle it shortens to \emph{recién}: \emph{recién llegado}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{recientemente} is built on \emph{reciente} and the ending \emph{-mente} (EtymDB). \emph{Reciente} is a learned word from Latin \emph{recēns} 'fresh, new'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[últimamente]{últimamente — lately}

\label{lesson:ES-C538-ultimamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for beforehand, then the Spanish for recently.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: últimamente}
\textbf{últimamente} — \textquotedblleft{}lately\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{últimamente} is built on \emph{último} and the ending \emph{-mente} (EtymDB). \emph{Último} is a learned word from Latin \emph{ultimus} 'farthest, last'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
